descriptor: Global insurer & asset manager · FY ends 31 December · reported in EUR

sections.title: Insurance & Capital Metrics
sections.subtitle: Allianz-specific disclosures: regulatory capital and P&C underwriting quality

charts.title: P&C Combined Ratio (partial history)
charts.annotation: Only disclosed for FY2013, FY2014 and FY2020 in the filings extracted so far — other years are gaps, not zeros.

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Allianz SE: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Allianz SE: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Allianz SE: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Allianz SE: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Allianz SE: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Allianz SE: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Operating profit and net income
profit.content:
Operating profit is Allianz's own headline earnings metric: underwriting result plus investment result plus fee income, before non-operating items such as realised gains/losses, impairments and acquisition-related costs. Net income is after those non-operating items, financing costs and tax.

For Allianz SE: management, analysts and the FY guidance range are all built on operating profit, not net income — the gap between the two lines is exactly the non-operating items operating profit is designed to exclude.

What to watch:

  • Operating profit tracking (or missing) the guided range given each February
  • A widening gap to net income from one-off items (e.g. the 2020 Covid-related impairments, disposal gains)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Allianz SE: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

solvencyRatio.title: Solvency II ratio
solvencyRatio.content:
The Solvency II ratio is eligible own funds divided by the regulatory solvency capital requirement, the EU insurance-sector capital-adequacy measure. Allianz targets roughly 150-220% as its comfort zone.

For Allianz SE: this is the capital buffer behind the dividend and buyback programme — a ratio falling toward the bottom of the target range is a precursor to slower capital return, not an immediate solvency concern given the regulatory minimum is 100%.

What to watch:

  • Trend relative to the ~150-220% target corridor
  • Market-driven swings (interest rates, equity markets) versus genuine capital generation

combinedRatio.title: P&C combined ratio
combinedRatio.content:
The combined ratio is claims incurred plus underwriting expenses, divided by net earned premiums, for the Property-Casualty segment. Below 100% means the underwriting business is profitable before investment income; above 100% means it relies on investment returns to be profitable overall.

For Allianz SE: only three years (FY2013, FY2014, FY2020) were extracted from the filings reviewed so far, so this chart is a partial history, not a continuous trend — FY2020's 96.3% reflects Covid-era claims and expense mix, not a structural deterioration.

What to watch:

  • Sustained readings above 100%
  • Natural-catastrophe years distorting a single year's ratio

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Allianz SE: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
